items.prompt: The prefix pre- means before. What does preheat mean?

options.why: Again is the meaning of re-.
Not is the meaning of un- or dis-.
Wrongly is the meaning of mis-.

hints: Look at the two parts of the word.
Cover pre- and read what is left.
Put the meaning of pre- together with heat.
items.explanation: Pre- means before. To preheat an oven means to heat it before you start cooking.

items.prompt: The prefix mis- means wrongly. What does misspell mean?

options.why: Again is the meaning of re-.
Before is the meaning of pre-.
Mis- means wrongly, not never.

hints: Find the prefix at the start of the word.
Cover mis- and read what is left.
Put the meaning of mis- together with spell.
items.explanation: Mis- means wrongly, so misspell means spell a word wrongly.

items.prompt:
Add mis- or pre- to counted.
Tom ___ the eggs, so he thought there were seven, not six.
hints: Did Tom get the right number?
Which prefix means wrongly?
Write the prefix, then the whole word counted.
items.explanation: Tom counted wrongly, so he miscounted. Mis- means wrongly.

items.prompt: Match each word to its meaning.
hints: Find the prefix in each word.
Pre- means before. Mis- means wrongly or badly.
Start with prepay. Which meaning has before in it and is about money?
items.explanation: Pre- means before, so prepay means pay before. Mis- means wrongly or badly, so misbehave means behave badly.

items.prompt: Sort the words. Which prefix makes a real word?
hints: Say each word with each prefix in front of it.
Only one of these prefixes makes a real word each time.
Start with spell. Is it prespell, misspell, unspell or disspell?
items.explanation: We say preheat and preview, misspell and misbehave, unfair and unlucky, disagree and disobey.

items.prompt: Before the film, our teacher showed us a short ___ so we knew what it was about.

options.why: Misview is not a word.
Unview is not a word.
Disview is not a word.

hints: The teacher showed it before the film.
Which prefix means before?
Try each prefix in front of view. Which one is a word you have heard?
items.explanation: Pre- means before. A preview is a short look at something before you see all of it.

items.prompt: Kemal ___ the question, so his answer was about the wrong thing.

options.why: Reread means read again. That would help him get it right!
Preread is not a word we use.
Unread means not read yet.

hints: What went wrong with Kemal's answer?
He read the question, but not in the right way.
Which prefix means wrongly?
items.explanation: Misread means read wrongly. Kemal misread the question, so his answer was about the wrong thing.

items.prompt:
Add mis- or pre- to behave.
Please do not ___ in the library.
hints: How should you act in a library?
You need a word that means behave badly.
Which prefix means wrongly or badly?
items.explanation: Misbehave means behave badly. Mis- means wrongly or badly.

items.prompt: Choose all the words where pre- means before.

options.why: Pre is just part of pretty. Tty is not a word.
Press is one whole word. Ss is not a word.
Prey is an animal hunted by another. Y is not a word.

hints: Cover pre at the start of each word.
Is the rest a real word?
If it is, check that before makes sense with it.
items.explanation: Preheat means heat before, preview means see before, and prehistoric means before history was written down. In pretty, press and prey, pre is just part of the word.

items.prompt: Ella ___ her keys and could not find them anywhere.

options.why: Replaced means put back, or swapped for a new one.
Preplaced is not a word we use.
Displaced means pushed out of its place. We need a word for lost.

hints: What happened to Ella's keys?
She put them somewhere, but in the wrong place.
Which prefix means wrongly?
items.explanation: Misplaced means put in the wrong place and lost. Mis- means wrongly.

items.prompt: Which word has a prefix that means wrongly?

options.why: Mist is one whole word. T is not a word.
Miss is one whole word.
Mister is one whole word. Ter is not a word.

hints: Cover mis at the start of each word.
Is the rest a real word?
If the rest is a word, does wrongly make sense with it?
items.explanation: Mishear is mis + hear, and it means hear wrongly. In mist, miss and mister, the letters mis are just part of the word.

options.why: Keep all of mis- and all of spell: mis + spell.
Spell ends with a double l.
There is only one p in spell.

hints: Think about the two parts of the word.
Write the prefix, then the root word, without dropping any letters.
Count the letter s where the two parts join.
items.explanation: Mis + spell = misspell. The prefix keeps its s and spell keeps its s, so there are two s letters together.
